title: Apothecary's Cellar
html:
The Apothecary's Cellar is a Location within the Blighted Village in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3.
“
A hidden laboratory full of abandoned experiments. Colour me in my element.
„
— Gale, entering the Necromancer's Lab

Overview

Access

The Apothecary's Cellar is located underneath the Blighted Village and is accessible from a hatch in the abandoned apothecary building, which is near the entrance of the village at coordinates X: 32 Y: 379. Inside the building behind the main counter on the floor is a Wooden Hatch through which the party can descend into the cellar.

Main Cellar

This section has a share of potions and alchemical ingredients scattered around in containers (mostly wooden barrels) and on the shelves, as well as in the wooden chest near the northern wall. On the desk next to the chest is a  Healer's Log and  Potion of Healing Recipe. Reading the former book helps to proceed into the Necromancer's Lab (see below).

A lever is hidden behind a stack of crates at X: -704 Y: -353. It is highlighted after passing a passive  DC 15 Perception Check, but can also be found through normal investigation. Pulling it opens a hidden passage behind a bookcase at X: -695 Y: -350, leading into the next chamber.

Cavernal Antechamber

“
The blacksmith. The teacher. The grocer. The baker. Little piggies to the butcher.
„
— Shovel, when asked about the identities of the guardians

This natural cavern has eight mouldering caskets scattered around. The casket closest to the tunnel entrance holds the  Scroll of Summon Quasit along with two bottles of  Alchemist's Fire and a  Poo-Scraper. The scroll can be used to cast the spell immediately, or transcribed by a  Wizard character.[1] Casting the spell summons  Shovel - previously the familiar of the former owner of the laboratory. Talking to her sheds some light onto the personality of her master.

Interacting with any of the other caskets caused a skeletal guardian to burst out of it,  surprising the party. Apart from attacking the party, the skeleton tries to run off to the other caskets, breaking them open and spawning more undead. There can possibly be three  Robust Guardians and four  Agile Guardians in total. Attacking any of the caskets still causes the skeletons to emerge, but without surprising the party.

Defeating all spawned skeletal guardians before they smash up remaining caskets prevents other guardians from appearing; extra xp and loot is then forfeited.

An effective strategy for dealing with the guardians is to drag all the caskets (by clicking and dragging) into a pile or stack and use  Cloud of Daggers or similar persistent ground attacks on them, breaking them all and wounding all guardians simultaneously and over multiple turns. This ensures loot and experience from all. Also, several fissured stalactites on the cavern vault can be shot down to damage whoever stands under them.

At X: -669 Y: -318 a passive  DC 15 Survival Check reveals hidden treasure. When the casket at X: -664 Y: -315 is opened or destroyed by a fellow guardian, a  Dark Journal falls out. Reading it reveals more information on the lab owner, progresses the ⁠Search the Cellar, and provides an additional option when interacting with the Ornate Mirror (see below).

At the south end of the cave is a wooden platform with a magical  Ornate Mirror on the wall. Interacting with it can open the way forward into the hidden lab. Convincing the mirror to let the party through earns the ⁠Mirror Master for the characters with the  Charlatan background.

Failing to convince the mirror causes it to unleash a floating flaming sphere which circles around the room, leaving a trail of fire. It takes a route throughout the cavern and partly into the tunnel leading in before losing power and returning into the mirror. The sphere attacks any object on sight, dealing 2d6⁠⁠Fire, with a  DC 12 Dexterity Saving Throw to halve the damage. After two appearances, its power dwindles, and it is possible to interact with the mirror again. This can be done as many times as needed.

For the details and possible dialogue options to operate the mirror, see the Ornate Mirror page. Also, the mirror can be destroyed by attacking it or choosing certain dialogue options.

Necromancer's Lab

The lab itself is a vast hall with the main workspace in the centre and several smaller rooms around it. Various containers in the lab and in the rooms contain alchemical ingredients, notably  Acorn Truffles, which can rarely be found freely while exploring.

In the centre of the lab there is an alchemists's workspace, where a  Scroll of Feather Fall and some  Basilisk Oil can be taken. Also, several documents and books describing the lab owner's concerns can be found.

The lesser rooms when coming around from most-eastern are:

  • A storeroom (almost across the entrance) with several containers with alchemical components. A lever in the far end moves a wall section to get back into the main cellar [2]. On the shelf is a  Rusted Key (Apothecary).
  • A room with a stuffed bear. A wooden chest at X: -679 Y: -370 contains several random scrolls.
  • A small library. The gilded chest at X: -656 Y: -369 contains the  Bracers of Defence.

On the east side is a gated off cavernous area which holds the real prize of this lab, the  Necromancy of Thay. A Marble Plate just before the rusted iron gate can be detected by a  DC 15 Perception Check. It activates the traps inside: two Gargoyle Statues on the each side and a pressure plate on which the tome itself is placed.

A  DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check can pick the gate lock, or the party can use the Rusted Key from the storeroom shelves. Alternatively, spells like  Misty Step or  Mage Hand can be used to bypass the gate. Each of the four traps here can be disabled with a  DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check. Otherwise, turn-based mode can be used to take the book and replace it with any other object, or simply rush out before the fire bolts from gargoyle statues are hurled.

The first interaction with the book updates the ⁠Search the Cellar quest, adding to the journal two subquests to it: ⁠Unlock the Ancient Tome and ⁠Destroy the Ancient Tome.  Astarion,  Karlach, and  Wyll may prompt their opinion on the tome, if they are in the party.

Once the  Dark Amethyst is acquired, any party member can try to read the tome, binding it to them permanently. The full list of possible interactions with the book, as well as companions' approval towards each of them, can be found at the  Necromancy of Thay page.

Rude, Crude, and Full of Attitude
Find and summon the quasit Shovel. Or is her name... Fork? Maybe Basket?

Notes
